source.title: Near-Duplicate Image Selection Transfers Preferences in Vision-Language Models
source.authors: Jaeyoung Kim; Eunseok Kim; Dongsuk Jang; Seunghyun Kim

page_placements.theme: Content-level checks fail to detect or remove the signal

record.tranche_reason: Tests preference transfer using a different method from the claim’s generated, filtered text: a teacher selects among precomputed near-duplicate images for fixed human captions, and students are evaluated without images. It also tests cross-checkpoint recipients and several robustness conditions.
record.gate_note: The paper’s central result bears on preference transfer, but its main intervention is image-variant selection, not training on teacher-generated numbers, code, or maths outputs. Source photographs and human captions are fixed, and the images are screened for target content; this is not the exact recipe in version A. The paper reports extensive training-grid, seed-repeat, caption-relay, and control results. The selected rows retain principal outcomes and key cross-checkpoint, JPEG-matching, full-fine-tuning, and prompt-sensitivity results; omitted result families are noted below.
record.test_reason: The study's own experiments test whether a curator's trained preference reaches fresh same-base students through semantically unrelated data. The channel is near-duplicate image choice with fixed human captions, and there is also a generated-caption relay. Owl, camel, oak and Reagan targets are measured by an image-free likelihood readout against matched neutral and sham students. It also runs cross-checkpoint recipients (B), JPEG-matching and gradient-alignment probes (D), and full fine-tuning plus alternative readouts (E). This is a different method aimed at version A's question, not the numbers/code/maths recipe.
record.authors_conclusion: Largely correct. Choosing among near-identical images, with photographs and human captions fixed, shifts same-base students' answer likelihoods toward the curator's preference. Strength depends on student training settings, and the preference can pass on through student-generated captions in LLaVA and Qwen3. Add three points. The measured transfer is a likelihood shift among fixed options, not seen in option-free generation. No cross-checkpoint condition transferred, which the authors call consistent with Cloud et al. The responsible features remain unresolved.
record.recipe_differences: The study uses a vision-language curation pipeline: a curator selects one of eight precomputed near-duplicate images using ordinary caption likelihood, while source photographs and human-written captions are fixed. Fresh students are fine-tuned on selected image-caption pairs. This differs from training on teacher-generated filtered number, code, or maths outputs.
record.method_sensitivity: Transfer varies with model, target, dataset size, update budget, learning rate, eligibility, student seed, source bank, and readout prompts. The paper reports that more updates can strengthen transfer, more sources at fixed updates can reduce it, and changing learning rate can alter both transfer and eligibility. Alternative preference prompt banks retain positive contrasts, whereas option-free generation shows no consistent increase.

fits_no_version.finding: Source-grouped linear probes on transformation parameters or CLIP embeddings predict the selecting arm at about 50% (LLaVA, Gemma) up to 59.7% (Qwen3).
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Detectability of subliminal-selection signals by content-level classifiers

record.code_released: Planned for release; URL not stated
record.problems: The transfer criterion is a descriptive decision rule, not a significance test, and has no calibrated false-positive rate or multiplicity control. Repeated student seeds reuse selected data, and within-bank blocks do not resample sources. Random-selection comparisons are descriptive rather than calibrated null tests. JPEG matching controls only JPEG-quality counts, leaving other transformation parameters unmatched. Cross-checkpoint conditions may differ in architecture, preprocessing, and recipe. Lexical filtering of captions does not exclude semantic cues. Some prompt-free evaluations show no consistent generation shift despite fixed-option likelihood shifts.
record.rows_left_out: To keep the record focused, not every result is separately rowed: detailed per-cell training-grid conditions and saved-checkpoint trajectories (Tables 25–30), additional student-seed repeats and target-rotation repeats (Table 11), all random-reselection draw values and pair-preserving assignments (Tables 18–21 and Appendix B.9), all caption-relay repeats and comparison routes (Tables 32–35), and exploratory classifier/readout aggregations (Tables 22–24 and 36–39) are omitted. These sections report additional setting-specific, repeat, or diagnostic results; the selected rows retain the primary transfer outcomes and central contrasts relevant to the claim.

untested.parts: Teacher-generated number lists, code and maths reasoning are not tested. The main route is selection among precomputed image variants. Only the caption relay (r13–r15) uses model-generated text, and it is filtered only lexically. Target curators are fine-tuned on constructed preference answers; naturally arising biases are untested.
There is no cross-base test with matched architecture, preprocessing and recipe, so the test cannot isolate shared initialization.
Entirely untested. The Reagan target is a preference among fixed options, not misalignment or harm.
Token entanglement, divergence tokens and steering-vector-like directions are not tested. The responsible image features are not identified.
Other LoRA ranks are not tested. Full fine-tuning is tested only for LLaVA students (curators stay LoRA) and at a different learning rate.
Entirely untested; there is no prompt-only intervention.

missing.what: Target rotations that meet the criterion in other models: LLaVA camel 0.082 and oak 0.095; Qwen3 camel 0.498 and oak 0.090 (all Met)

Training grid on a disjoint 40K reservoir. The 8K recipe meets the criterion in LLaVA (.107) and Qwen3 (.355) but not Qwen2.5 (.071, h .111). More updates strengthen transfer; more sources at fixed updates reduce it. LLaVA's eligible reversal (−.216) did not reproduce on re-run.
Students of 50%-target curators: contrasts are smaller than target-only in 48/48 pairs; no model meets the dispersion criterion
LLaVA development runs: K=2 candidates not met (.036); 50% and 25% curated-data mixtures not met (.050, .046)
Student-seed repeats: Qwen2.5 oak meets the criterion in 1/3 sets, Qwen2.5 camel 2/3, Qwen3 oak 2/3; all others 3/3
Second-generation student image reselection does not meet the criterion in LLaVA (.001) or Qwen2.5 (.058). Curator-caption routes give very large contrasts (LLaVA 1.556, Qwen3 22.13, Qwen2.5 3.461).
Pair-preserving random assignment in Qwen3-VL gives signed contrasts of about .01–.02 nats, against an original of .362

Readout sensitivity: the criterion holds in 19/21 conditions on the main readout, 15/21 on normalized share and 11/21 on tie-split argmax. Alternative answer forms meet the criterion in 10/18; the full-name form fails for all political targets.
LLaVA frozen-projector LoRA students also meet the criterion (Ē 0.1207, h 0.0224)

record.verdict_notes: Changes from the reader's record. r16–r19 moved from limits_scope to supports for A, since target selection beats random reselection. r20–r21 relinked to D only and set to absent. Cross-checkpoint rows r22–r25 set to observed for B, since B predicts failure. The reader's B limits_scope label was dropped: the confound caveat is an interpretive limit, not a result. The Qwen2.5 main owl run was a follow-up after its selector screen failed. LLaVA's political-target condition is pipeline-invalid (decoding-limit rate 5.47%). The transfer criterion is descriptive, with no calibrated false-positive rate.

versions.untested_parts: Does not test filtered teacher-generated number lists, code, or maths reasoning. Its main route is curator selection among near-duplicate image variants paired with fixed human captions.

Tests four cross-checkpoint recipient conditions, but architecture, preprocessing, and training recipe can also differ; the paper says these results do not establish that shared initialization is necessary.
No misalignment or other harmful alignment-relevant trait is tested. The political-target experiment measures preference for Ronald Reagan among candidate answers, not harmful behavior.

Explores JPEG-quality matching and an initial-gradient alignment probe, but does not identify the responsible signal or test token entanglement, divergence tokens, or a steering-vector-like direction.
Tests full language-model and projector fine-tuning for LLaVA students and alternative readout prompts. It does not test other LoRA ranks.
